subject: maths
chapter_title: The Mathematics of Maybe: Introduction to Probability

concepts.title: What Is Probability
concepts.definition: Probability puts a number on uncertainty: it measures how likely an event is on a scale from 0 for the impossible to 1 for the certain, so statements like likely or unlikely become exact fractions between these poles.
concepts.key_idea: Uncertainty becomes arithmetic: 0 impossible, 1 certain, fractions in between.
question_patterns: define probability in your own words
what is the probability of an impossible event
what is the probability of a certain event
can the probability of an event exceed 1 - justify
assign the given events their positions on the probability scale
explain the mathematics of maybe with an example

solution_steps.explain: Impossible events get 0; sure events get 1.
Real events sit between as proper fractions.
Closer to 1 means more likely; closer to 0 means less likely.

concepts.title: Measuring Probability Objectively
concepts.definition: When all outcomes are equally likely, probability is measured objectively as the ratio of favourable outcomes to total outcomes - tossing a fair coin gives one head among two outcomes, a probability of one half.
concepts.key_idea: Count fair: favourable outcomes over all equally likely outcomes.
question_patterns: find the probability of getting a head when a fair coin is tossed
a die is rolled once - find the probability of a number greater than 4
find the probability of drawing a red ball from the given bag
what is the probability of the complement of the given event
out of the given cards find the probability of the stated draw
compute the probability of getting at least one head in two tosses

solution_steps.explain: All equally likely outcomes form the denominator.

concepts.title: Tree Diagrams for Combined Experiments
concepts.definition: When an experiment has stages - like tossing two coins or drawing twice - a tree diagram lays out every path of outcomes; counting the branches that favour the event and dividing by all branches gives its probability.
concepts.key_idea: Branch by branch: the tree turns a compound experiment into a countable list.
question_patterns: draw a tree diagram for tossing two coins and list the outcomes
how many outcomes does the given two-stage experiment have
use the tree diagram to find the probability of the given event
in the tree of two draws which branches favour the event
list the sample space of the given compound experiment
why does a tree diagram prevent missing outcomes

solution_steps.explain: One level of branches per stage of the experiment.
Every root-to-tip path is one outcome of the combined experiment.
Favourable paths over total paths give the probability.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A fair coin is tossed. Find the probability of the event with {favourable_count} favourable outcome(s) out of {total} outcomes.
A die is rolled once. Find the probability of the event having {favourable_count} favourable faces out of {total}.

solution_template.explain: Favourable over total gives the chance.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The probability of an event is {probability}. Find the probability that it does not happen.

solution_template.explain: The complement takes the remaining share of certainty.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If the chance of rain today is {probability}, what is the chance that it does not rain?
